messages:
sophia: FYI - AcmeCo reported their private VPC endpoints started failing after our cert rotation last night. Their API calls to their private hostname return TLS errors.
sophia: Error they sent: `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` and `remote error: tls: bad certificate`.
acme-support: Confirmed. This was working until about 02:10 UTC when we deployed the new intermediate. No other infra changes on their side.
akash: Can you paste the curl + openssl checks they ran? Need to see the cert chain from the server.
sophia: They ran:
```
$ curl -v https://private.acme.internal:443
* SSL connection using TLS1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* server certificate verification OK
* CAfile: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
* TLS error: certificate signed by unknown authority
```
And openssl:
```
$ openssl s_client -showcerts -connect private.acme.internal:443
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = private.acme.internal
verify error:num=19:self signed certificate in certificate chain
verify return:1
...\n---
certificate chain
1 s:/CN=Private Int CA
  i:/CN=Root CA
---
```
pranav: That "self signed certificate in certificate chain" usually means the server presented an incomplete chain or a mismatched intermediate. Did we accidentally drop the intermediate or reorder certs on the gateway?
acme-support: We inspected their LB (NGINX) and it has the new leaf + intermediate configured, but cert order was leaf, root, intermediate. We corrected to leaf + intermediate + root -> still failing.
akash: Two possibilities: 1) client trust store is missing the intermediate/root, 2) server is presenting a wrong intermediate or using a cert signed by a different intermediate than the trust store expects.
sophia: The customer uses a hardened VPC with strict egress allowlist. Could they be blocking OCSP/CRL fetch which makes some clients reject chain? Also their app validates differently than curl.
pranav: Good call. But openssl s_client does full chain verification locally and already showed verify error 19. That is before OCSP. So likely a chain presentation issue. Can they run `openssl x509 -noout -text -in <intermediate.pem>` to confirm issuer/subject match?
acme-support: Running that now. Also sharing the full server cert block:
```
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIF...leaf...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIF...root...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```
akash: I spot the problem — they pasted root directly after leaf, missing the intermediate. If LB served leaf+root only, some clients won't be able to build chain to trusted anchor unless the intermediate is known locally.
sophia: They think the intermediate was rotated to a new int CA yesterday. Maybe some of their nodes still have old cached intermediate and are presenting inconsistent chains depending on which node handles traffic.
acme-support: We checked multiple nodes; 3/5 present leaf+root, 2/5 present leaf+intermediate+root. The ones with only root are failing.
pranav: Sounds like a partially rolled update. Plan: (1) ensure every LB/nginx has the full bundle in correct order: leaf then intermediate(s) then root. (2) restart/reload to clear any in-memory cert cache. (3) confirm via `openssl s_client -showcerts` from outside their VPC and from a host inside their VPC.
akash: Also check their VPC NAT/egress rules — if some nodes are fetching the intermediate from our CA endpoint during rotation and fail due to blocked egress, they might revert to a fallback config. But primary fix is uniform bundle.
sophia: I opened ticket INF-8345 and escalated to infra oncall. Logged repro steps and included failing host list + partial node inventory. ETA for customer-facing note?
acme-support: Customer requested an ETA. If infra can push a uniform cert bundle and reload within the hour, we'll tell them 60-90 mins.
oncall-bot: INF-8345 assigned to akash. Priority: P1. Estimated ack by 5m.
akash: Acknowledged. I'll push a config update to the 2 nodes with the bad bundle, reload nginx, and run `openssl s_client` tests. Will report back.
pranav: After it's fixed, recommend adding a post-rotation verification checklist: 1) verify bundle order everywhere, 2) verify no nodes fall back to old certs, 3) run synthetic curl+openssl from both public and private subnets, 4) check egress allowlists for CA/CRL/OCSP endpoints.
sophia: Thanks — keeping customer updated. I'll post the final confirmation here when infra reports success.
acme-support: Thanks team. Customer appreciates rapid response. :thumbsup:
